sections.label: The story of your project this year

content.text:
During this reporting period, we delivered the project around a clear community purpose: supporting isolated and vulnerable families and young people in Beeston and Holbeck so they could experience improved wellbeing and social connection.

Our work was shaped by the differences we were trying to make. We focused on helping families feel less isolated and more connected to support. We also provided safe after-school spaces for young people, while creating opportunities for volunteers to gain confidence and help shape community activity.

The records submitted for this section did not include delivery totals, attendance figures, spend data, or year-specific learning evidence. Because of that, we have described the project story in line with the confirmed objectives and outcomes, but we have not added unsupported numbers or detail.

sections.label: The differences you are making, both big and small

content.text:
We reported this work against the differences we set out to make for isolated and vulnerable families and young people in Beeston and Holbeck. Those intended differences were improved wellbeing and social connection, with a focus on families feeling less isolated and more connected to support, young people having safe after-school spaces, and volunteers gaining confidence while helping shape community activity.

During the reporting period, we recruited and supported 14 community volunteers against a target of 18. This showed solid progress, but it was below target by 4. The records available for this progress update confirmed the volunteer figure, but they did not explain the reason for the shortfall.

We also had a proposal target to collect 20 short parent or carer feedback comments. However, the submitted records available for this section did not include the actual number collected, so we have not stated an achievement figure where evidence was missing.

More broadly, the evidence submitted for this section did not include beneficiary numbers or story-based examples that could be reported with confidence. As a result, we have stayed close to the verified records rather than filling gaps with unsupported detail. Even with those limits, the volunteer data and the stated outcome framework show that the project remained focused on reducing isolation, offering safe spaces, and strengthening local volunteer involvement.

content.text:
During this progress update period, our learning stayed closely tied to the differences we were trying to make. Our work was grounded in the aim that isolated and vulnerable families and young people in Beeston and Holbeck experience improved wellbeing and social connection. We also worked toward families feeling less isolated and more connected to support, young people having safe after-school spaces, and volunteers gaining confidence and helping shape community activity.

From the evidence available, the clearest learning was about the importance of maintaining safe spaces and trusted support for families and young people who were isolated, anxious or struggling. That focus remained consistent with the outcomes we had set out at the start of the project, and it gave us a clear frame for judging whether activity was relevant and useful.

We can also see from the records that sessional youth workers were a planned part of delivery, with a budget line of £13,600. That suggests staffed youth provision was treated as an important element of creating safe after-school space for young people. However, the submitted records for this section did not include confirmed narrative evidence on what worked best, what did not work as expected, any unexpected findings, or what may be useful to others.

Because those reflections were not available in the submitted material, we have not added further detail here. We have instead reported only what can be supported by the current evidence base.
